analysis: What changed vs the 5am brief: (1) CoreWeave got worse again - premarket now -4% to -5.5% (~$66-67) vs -3.6% to -4.4% at 5am, and WSJ's Friday coverage widened the frame: CreditSights expects ~$80B of cash burn over 3.5 years against $35B+ of debt; CDS at all-time highs; some unsecured bonds below 80 cents; Citrini's Thursday note observed market cap ($36.3B) roughly equals debt ($36.6B), meaning bondholders get paid in full if equity loses half. The credit-led thesis keeps winning over Huang's defense. (2) Anthropic is the NEW signal: Reuters exclusive (Oct 15) says IPO investors are discussing ~$1.5T valuation vs the ~$2T expected for the November sale, after Q3 revenue growth slowed sequentially ($16.8B, +45% q/q, vs a doubling in Q2) despite adjusted profitability. The AI-financing repricing is now hitting the demand side (model labs' growth/valuations), not just the supply-side debt (neoclouds). Single-source (four anonymous people), treat as fragile until confirmed. (3) Tesla's pop STRENGTHENED: +3% to +5.1% premarket with actual product details (SpaceX cold-gas thrusters; invite-only one-seater with brief flight; 2028 production; no price; reservations reopened) - but the durability question remains: spectacle vs. Oct 21 earnings. (4) Warsh gave the market what it wanted by saying nothing: 'doesn't prejudge meetings,' declined to endorse the no-rush signals; Oct hike odds dropped to 15% from 28% yesterday. Signal: AI-financing repricing broadening from neocloud debt to model-lab valuations (CoreWeave + Anthropic in one morning); SOX potentially facing its longest losing run since 2008. Noise: Roadster market-cap math, SpaceX merger chatter, premarket single-stock pops (NVR/COO laggards, Alcoa/JBHT earnings movers).
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures near-flat ~30 min before the bell: S&P 500 +0.1%, Dow +0.2%, Nasdaq 100 flat to -0.1% (Investopedia/WSJ, <1h). The SOX is at risk of an eighth straight down day - its longest losing run since October 2008 (WSJ, <1h). Asia rebounded overnight: Kospi +2.05% after Thursday's 7.6% plunge (week -14.5%), Nikkei +1.8%, Taiex +0.55%; Stoxx 600 +0.5%. 10Y ~5.11-5.12% (+~5bps from Thursday's 5.07% close); 2Y ~4.76%. CME: October hike odds 15% (down from 28% yesterday), December hike 89%. Week-to-date: Nasdaq -2.4% (four-week streak ending), S&P -0.9%, Dow +1%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A calmer but unresolved tape - the defensive rotation held overnight, yet the SOX 8-day streak watch and the Nasdaq red show AI-credit stress is still the dominant frame; 8:30/9:15 ET data lands with the blackout starting Saturday.

headlines.headline: Tesla +3% to +5.1% premarket after the Roadster reveal (Barron's/Investopedia, <1h): two-seater with SpaceX cold-gas thrusters boosting acceleration; invite-only one-seater with downward thrusters enabling brief flight (not road-legal); production targeted 2028; no price disclosed; reservations reopened (CNBC via Investopedia). SpaceX +2.1% to +2.5%. HSBC: 'an engineering flex rather than a demonstration of earnings power.'
headlines.why_it_matters: The halo strengthened with real product detail, but HSBC's framing plus the still-speculative SpaceX merger chatter (single-source, no confirmation) means the pop is priced on spectacle - Oct 21 earnings is the real test.

headlines.headline: CoreWeave -4% to -5.5% premarket (~$66-67), on track for a ~20% weekly drop - its worst since November 2025 (WSJ live, <1h). New context from WSJ's Friday deep-dive: CreditSights sees ~$80B of cash burn over the next 3.5 years against $35B+ of debt; CDS at all-time highs; some unsecured bonds below 80 cents. Citrini (Thursday): market cap ($36.3B) roughly equals debt ($36.6B) - bondholders are paid in full even if equity loses half; either a great investment or 'the entire AI complex is at risk of a rug-pull.' CFO Nitin Agrawal sold ~$1.8M of shares near $80 Monday via a 10b5-1 plan (MarketWatch).
headlines.why_it_matters: The credit-led thesis keeps beating the equity-defense thesis: bond desks are repricing AI-linked debt as a class, and the CFO's own share sales undercut the 'we're fine' message - this remains the tape's central risk signal.

headlines.headline: Anthropic IPO investors tempering valuation expectations: Reuters exclusive (Oct 15) says some current and prospective IPO investors discussed ~$1.5T valuation vs the ~$2T previously expected for the November share sale, after Q3 revenue growth slowed sequentially ($16.8B, +45% q/q; adjusted profitable) vs a doubling in Q2. Based on four anonymous people; Anthropic did not respond to comment requests.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed - treat as fragile. But if it holds, the AI-financing repricing has spread from neocloud debt to the model labs' own growth expectations, and Reuters flags the November IPO as the near-term bellwether for the whole AI market.

headlines.headline: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, speaking overnight at an IMF meeting in Bangkok, declined to signal whether the central bank will hold or hike at the Oct 27-28 meeting ('doesn't prejudge meetings'), and would not endorse colleagues' no-rush signals (WSJ, <1h). Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid: 'The most important thing was what [Warsh] didn't say. Markets took the lack of hawkishness as good news.' October hike odds fell to 15% from 28% yesterday (CME). Friday macro: import/export prices 8:30 ET, industrial production & capacity utilization 9:15 ET; today is the last day of Fed speak before Saturday's blackout.
headlines.why_it_matters: Warsh's non-signal did the dovish work without committing - odds of an October surprise keep falling, which supports equities but leaves the December-hike debate to Friday's data and the blackout.
